title: docs(adr): ADR-0019 D3 amended — a suite may surface several apps, each defined by a different package; an app package still defines at most one app
body:
Fixes #32585

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：ADR-0019 的 D3 从「一个套件折叠成一个应用」改成「一个套件可以露出几个应用，每个包最多一个应用，各放各的」。D3 下新增一段修订说明：规则、三条理由、「应用包 / 模块 / 应用 / 套件」四个叫法的对照表。状态行、后续事项、代价三处写着「HotCRM 折成一个应用」的句子划掉并改写。`type: app` 不改名，D1、D2 不动（D1 下加了一条带日期的说明：套件里用户「打开」的是其中一个应用）。
- **为什么改**：您在 #32585 裁定「改成 Salesforce 模式」：HotCRM 的销售、服务、营销三个应用分别放在主包、服务包、营销包里。原 D3 禁止这种形态，不修订的话这个方案只能靠检查的缺口落地。
- **风险与回滚**：纯文档，不动代码、不动契约；回滚即 revert 本 PR。两处与卡面不完全一样，请留意：① 理由二「应用不能引用别的包的对象」只在「本包自己定义了对象」时才由构建检查；实测有两种情况不受这条检查约束：包里一个对象都没有，或者导航项写了 `requiresObject`。修订文照实写了，没有把构建说得比实际更严；② 「模块包最多一个应用」今天代码还不拦（实测模块包放两个应用能通过构建），执行在 #32586，修订文写明「已声明、未执行」。
- **先看**：只有一个文件 `docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`。先看 D3 下「Amendment note」里的「The rule」和三条理由（理由二最长）；再看同一段末尾的「Records that restate D3」（ADR-0130、ADR-0141 里说 D3 未修订的旧句子现在怎么读）。
- **两分钟验证**：打开本 PR 的 Files changed，预期只有这一个文件；D3 标题里旧标题带删除线，新标题是「A suite may surface several apps, at most one per package」；对照表四行，中文、英文叫法各一列。
- **需要你做的**:审阅并合并本 PR(`docs/adr/**` 属 Tier H,由您亲手合并)。契约复核 PASS:首轮 6818867679,增量复核 6819399847,`Head-sha: 82729d78f4773519a86752792c3c85db7ee97a4b`。

## What changes

One file, `docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md` (162 insertions, 8 deletions; 181 lines before, 335 after). No accepted sentence is deleted: a sentence the ruling reverses is struck through and stays readable.

**The four items the card rules**

1. **D3 amended.** The heading keeps its number; its old title is struck and the new one reads "A suite may surface several apps, at most one per package (no aggregator above App; amended 2026-11-12)". The second sentence of D3 (a vertical solution "MUST resolve to one App") is struck with a dated pointer. The label "(suite)" in its first sentence is struck too, and the note says why. A dated amendment note at the end of the section carries the rule exactly as the card states it: "A suite (one install: an app package plus the module packages it composes) MAY surface more than one app, provided each app is defined by a different package of the suite, and an app package defines at most one app. A product that is genuinely independent still ships as its own app package (the iWork route stays)." The note opens with the two rulings, verbatim and untranslated: 「改成 Salesforce 模式」 and 「同意」.
2. **The three reasons, with citations.** The Console addresses an app by its package id; an app may not name another package's object, where its own package defines objects; disabling a module removes the app that module owns. Each cites the code that makes it true as a symbol anchor (see Acceptance notes 1 to 4 for where the text differs from the card's).
3. **One terminology table**, four rows, Chinese and English: `type: app` package = 应用包 (主包 in a suite) / app package; `type: module` package = 模块 / module; an entry in `apps[]` = 应用 / app; one install of an app package with its modules = 套件 / suite, a descriptive word, not a package type. `type: app` is not renamed.
4. **The two stale lines.** The status line's Pending clause no longer says "HotCRM folded to a single App (D3/D4)"; it names the check on #32586 and HotCRM's split, and the line gains an **Amended** segment. The Consequences line "HotCRM and any existing suite-style packages must fold to a single App (D3/D4)" is struck and rewritten.

**Written by the dev around those four, so the record does not contradict itself** (each is one short dated line or paragraph; strike any you do not want)

- In the note: what is reversed and what stands (D1 and D2 unchanged, "one marketplace listing still installs one app package"; D4 not amended); what is enforced today and what is not yet, including that the build does not require an app to sit in the package of the objects it shows; what is not decided (option C; per-position app visibility and default app); how ADR-0130 D2 and ADR-0141 read from now; where the accepted text uses "suite" in its earlier sense.
- Where the record restated the fold: a Revision history bullet, a note under Context (the target changes inside one install, nothing moves at the listing), a note under D1 (its rule is not amended; "opens" reads differently for a suite), a note under D4 (its last sentence illustrates the fold), the Scope follow-up (struck), a note under Consequences / Positive ("install = open = uninstall" for a suite), a fourth entry in Alternatives considered (A, B′ and C as offered), and one References line.

**House style followed, and why.** The most recent reversal of an accepted decision by a maintainer ruling is ADR-0093 D8.1 (ruling 6796108313, on `main` since `e5428312`): the reversed sentence is struck with a dated pointer, the new rule sits in a dated "Amendment note" blockquote at the end of the decision's section, the status line gains an **Amended** segment, and every place that restates the reversed rule gets a dated pointer. This PR follows that shape. ADR-0150's notes use the same blockquote form, and the heading follows ADR-0053 D-D1 (old words struck, "(amended DATE)" appended). D3 is not rewritten in place with the old text removed, because no amendment in the registry deletes a ruled sentence and ADR-0130 D2 states the convention ("a governed record is amended by an additive addendum").

**`docs/adr/README.md` is not touched.** The index prints only the first 75 characters of a status line, and this edit starts after them. On this head `node scripts/adr-index.mjs --check` answers "docs/adr/README.md is current" (Acceptance note 7).

No changeset: `docs/adr/**` ships in no package, so the PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## Tests

No test changes: prose only, no behaviour moves. Local gates on head `82729d78` (the branch with `origin/main` at `8bfbc4ed` merged in): the 21 families `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives, each exit 0, reconciled by `--ran` as "21 derived, 21 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". One-time probe of `defineStack` (not committed) for the readings the note marks "(probed)".

## Acceptance notes

1. **The card's two line citations are written as symbol and file anchors.** The card cites `appRoute.ts` by a line range and HotCRM's `crm.app.ts` by a line. `pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors` refuses a line number anywhere in `docs/adr/**` (a hard `[line-anchor]` finding). So the note cites `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/appRoute.ts#appRouteSegment`, `#matchAppBySegment` and `#appAddressSegment`, which are what the card's range covers, and cites HotCRM at file level in the cross-repo form ADR-0142 uses (`hotcrm:src/sales/apps/crm.app.ts`).
2. **HotCRM was not opened.** This session has no access to that repository (the read answered 403), so the HotCRM file and the hotcrm plan (M11, hotcrm#2417 comment 6814732293) are cited as the card cites them. Their content is not verified here.
3. **Reason 2 is narrower than the card's sentence, and the note says exactly how narrow.** The navigation check runs only under the strict parse (the default) and only in a package that defines at least one object. There, `defineStack` refuses an app's own navigation entry that names an object the package does not define, and keeps refusing it when `artifactObjects` lists that object. Two shapes pass: a package that defines no object is not checked at all (`validateCrossReferences` returns early; the code names this leniency as deliberate and `stack.test.ts` pins it), and an entry that declares `requiresObject` is skipped. So the card's "An app may not name another package's object" carries "where its own package defines objects", and its "An app housed apart from its objects is a shell that only contributions can fill" reads "an app housed in a package that defines objects, but not the objects it shows, is a shell that only contributions, or entries gated by `requiresObject`, can fill". The note proposes no change to either leniency. Found by contract review 6818867679 (F1); probe output under Verification.
4. **Reasons 1 and 3 gain this repository's own anchors.** For reason 1 the note adds ADR-0048 §3.1 (the package id is the route key) and the server's reading of the same key (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-scope.ts#resolveAppPackageIdKey`: a package that holds more than one app answers as absent when read by its package id). For reason 3 the card cites only the hotcrm plan; the note adds the two mechanisms on this tree (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts#isDisableableAppModule`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-refusals.ts#isItemOfDisabledPackage`). Both were read from the code, not run.
5. **The module half of the rule is declared, not enforced.** Probed: an app package with two apps is refused (`STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`); a module package with two apps is accepted. The note states this and names #32586 as the check. It also states that the build does not require an app to sit in the package of the objects it shows: reasons 2 and 3 argue for that placement, nothing checks it.
6. **Text outside this card's file surface still describes the fold.** Left alone, and noted here, not filed: ADR-0130 D2 ("ADR-0019 D1–D3 stand verbatim and unamended", "the suite ADR-0019 D3 removed by name", "exactly one consumer-visible consequence"), its Non-goals and its alternative 5; ADR-0141's "Unchanged" line; `docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md` ("refolded into a single consumer App", and "one App ... or several independent Apps — never a suite"). The spec prose that says an app package defines at most one app stays true as written.
7. **The index needs no regeneration.** On this head, with `origin/main` at `8bfbc4ed` merged in, `node scripts/adr-index.mjs --check` exits 0: "docs/adr/README.md is current and every record parsed". `pnpm check:adr-index` prints no stale warning.
8. **One word, one meaning.** The label "(suite)" in D3's first sentence is struck, because the table gives the word a different meaning. The narrative sections (Context, Out of scope, Consequences, Alternatives 1 and 2) keep their accepted wording, and the vocabulary paragraph says so.
9. **Not in this amendment**, as the card rules: several apps in one `type: app` package (option C), and per-position app visibility or a per-position default app.

## Verification

<details><summary>One-time probe of defineStack on the merged head (scratch test, deleted after the reading)</summary>

Run under the verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` on one scratch file under `packages/spec/src`, 1 test file, 1 test passed. `packages/spec` is byte-identical to `main` at `8bfbc4ed` on this branch.

```text
PROBE app-package-two-apps {"accepted":false,"code":"STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION","firstIssue":"An 'app' package must define at most one app, but found 2 (app_a, app_b). Fold them into one app with multiple"}
PROBE module-package-two-apps {"accepted":true}
PROBE with-object/app-nav-foreign-object {"accepted":false,"code":"STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID","firstIssue":"App 'app_a' navigation references object 'demo_case' which is not defined in objects."}
PROBE with-object/app-nav-foreign-object+artifactObjects {"accepted":false,"code":"STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID","firstIssue":"App 'app_a' navigation references object 'demo_case' which is not defined in objects."}
PROBE with-object/app-nav-foreign-object+requiresObject {"accepted":true}
PROBE with-object/module-nav-foreign-object {"accepted":false,"code":"STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID","firstIssue":"App 'app_a' navigation references object 'demo_case' which is not defined in objects."}
PROBE no-object/app-nav-foreign-object (objects key absent) {"accepted":true}
PROBE no-object/app-nav-foreign-object (objects: []) {"accepted":true}
PROBE no-object/module-nav-foreign-object {"accepted":true}
```

</details>

<details><summary>Readings from the code on main at 8bfbc4ed</summary>

- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: `validateSingleApp` returns no finding unless `manifest.type` is `app`. `validateCrossReferences` returns its findings at `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;` before it reaches the navigation walk; the walk judges an app navigation entry's `objectName` against the stack's own objects and skips an entry that declares `requiresObject`. The text above `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors` names the early return as the one leniency it inherits ("that stack's references may be served by a plugin that is not in this composition at all"). The `artifactObjects` option's own text says an app's navigation stays refused against the stack's own objects. `defineStack` skips validation when `strict` is `false`.
- `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts`: "should skip cross-reference validation when no objects are defined" pins the early return; "does not constrain non-app package types" pins a `driver` package with two apps as accepted.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/appRoute.ts`: `appRouteSegment` returns the package id, `matchAppBySegment` returns the first app that carries it, and the text above `appAddressSegment` says the name stays the only address that reaches the others.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-scope.ts`: `resolveAppPackageIdKey` returns the request unchanged, so the read answers absence, when the package holds more than one app.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`: `isDisableableAppModule` is true for a `module` package that directly declares an installed `app` package.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-refusals.ts`: `isItemOfDisabledPackage` judges a non-object item by its own package id; the list read and the by-name read both ask it.

Every file named here is byte-identical between `874166b6`, where the first round read it, and this head (`git diff --quiet`, exit 0).

</details>
